latest.issue: The test `test_shim_markers_cpp_asserts_every_marker` looks for the literal substring `static_assert(<marker> == 1`. Step 7's `make format` breaks that substring for the card's own kernel globals marker. If the implementer skips formatting, `make lint` fails instead, so `make test` and `make lint` cannot both pass.
latest.evidence:
I ran `.venv/bin/clang-format` 18.1.8 with the repo `.clang-format` on the line from shim_markers.cpp step 2. It becomes:
```
static_assert(
    PAINTERLY_SHIM_KERNEL_DEVICE_CPU_GLOBALS_H == 1,
    "kernel/device/cpu/globals.h did not resolve to src/cycles/shim/kernel/device/cpu/globals.h");
```
The message is too long to align after `static_assert(`, so clang-format breaks right after the parenthesis. The substring `static_assert(PAINTERLY_SHIM_KERNEL_DEVICE_CPU_GLOBALS_H == 1` is then missing from the file. Left unwrapped, the line is about 158 columns, and `clang-format --dry-run --Werror` (the `make lint` recipe) rejects it. Shorter markers such as `util/param.h` stay on one line, which is why the problem only shows up for this marker.
latest.fix: In "Modify" › `tests/core/test_shims.py` and in "Shim markers", make the match whitespace-insensitive: `re.search(rf"static_assert\(\s*{re.escape(marker)}\s*==\s*1\s*,", text)`. Add a sentence saying that clang-format may wrap the `static_assert` and the test ignores whitespace. Optionally also shorten the message pattern, e.g. `"<path>: shim not reached"`, so most lines stay on one line.

latest.issue: T6.3 is the first card to compile Cycles' type-punning byte-code read, and it does so without the compiler flag Blender always uses for that code. `svm_node_get<T>` reinterprets the `uint` `svm_nodes` array as typed node structs and reads float, enum and `PackedTransform` members through it. Under ISO C++ strict aliasing that is undefined behaviour. Blender builds Cycles with `-fno-strict-aliasing`; Painterly's build adds only `-ffp-contract=off -fno-fast-math`. The verbatim code therefore runs in a compile environment that upstream never uses, while the card claims bit-exact results.
latest.evidence:
Upstream code:

Blender v5.2.2 platform files (fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com, tag v5.2.2):
- `build_files/cmake/platform/platform_unix.cmake:898` (GCC) and `:970` (Clang): `set(PLATFORM_CFLAGS "-pipe -fPIC -funsigned-char -fno-strict-aliasing -ffp-contract=off")`;
- `platform_apple.cmake:161`: the same flags;
- `platform_win32.cmake:207` (clang-cl): `/clang:-fno-strict-aliasing`.

Painterly: the root `CMakeLists.txt:22` adds only `-ffp-contract=off -fno-fast-math`. Neither `src/cycles/CMakeLists.txt` nor any M6a draft mentions strict aliasing (grep over cards/M6a/*.md finds nothing).

This card's doctests write every struct with `memcpy`, so a miscompile is unlikely here. M6b and T6.5 feed byte code that SVMCompiler writes with `reinterpret_cast<const int *>(&node)` (scene/svm.h:104), which has no such protection.

```cmake
  target_compile_options(cycles_kernel INTERFACE -fno-strict-aliasing)
endif()
```
Attaching it to `cycles_kernel` gives every kernel consumer one flag set (`cycles_svm`, `cycles_svm_headers_check`, `painterly_tests`, and later `cycles_scene`). The flag changes no layout and no floating-point result, so the hashes, the generated-header sha256 and the expected values stay valid.
